quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian shepherds developed a unique breed of dog called the Puli, famous for its distinctive corded coat that looks like dreadlocks. These intelligent herding dogs were so valued that a shepherd would pay a full year's salary to acquire one. The cords naturally form as the dog matures and help protect them from harsh weather and predators.

short_read.title: How Hummingbirds Get Their Incredible Colors
short_read.teaser: Hummingbirds don't actually have colorful feathers—their brilliant hues come from microscopic structures that bend light like tiny prisms. Scientists have discovered the remarkable physics behind these dazzling displays.

medium_read.title: The Libraries That Survived the Ancient World
medium_read.teaser: Before the internet and printing presses, great libraries preserved humanity's knowledge on fragile scrolls and tablets. Discover the fascinating stories of ancient libraries from Alexandria to Nineveh and how their contents were saved or lost to time.

long_read.title: The Secret Language of Trees
long_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that trees communicate through underground fungal networks, sharing nutrients and warning each other of danger. This groundbreaking research reveals that forests are far more social and intelligent than we ever imagined.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season Continues
port_angeles.description: Late August is still prime time to spot harbor seal pups along the shores of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Ediz Hook and the rocky beaches near Dungeness are favorite haul-out spots where mothers nurse their pups. Remember to watch from a distance—these adorable babies need space to rest and bond with their mothers.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You know your hummingbird facts! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power their hovering flight.
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! Their hearts beat about 1,200 times per minute—that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are amazing—they beat about 1,200 times per minute during flight, which helps power their incredible hovering abilities!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To support such a rapid heartbeat, hummingbirds must eat constantly, consuming up to twice their body weight in nectar each day. Their metabolism is so fast that they enter a hibernation-like state called torpor at night to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm! That's right! Such a beautiful word to express gratitude.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Köszönöm'—such a lovely word! 'Szia' means hello, 'Viszlát' means goodbye, and 'Igen' means yes.
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it quite different from surrounding European languages. It's related to Finnish and Estonian rather than German, Slavic, or Romance languages.

puzzle_3.question: What is the largest species of seal found in the Strait of Juan de Fuca?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Steller sea lions are magnificent creatures—males can weigh up to 2,500 pounds and are often seen on the rocks near Race Rocks and Protection Island!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is Steller sea lion! While harbor seals are common, these impressive sea lions are the largest pinnipeds in our area, with males weighing up to 2,500 pounds.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Steller sea lions are named after Georg Wilhelm Steller, the naturalist on Vitus Bering's 1741 expedition to Alaska. Their population in the Pacific Northwest has been recovering after being listed as endangered, and they're now a thrilling sight around the Olympic Peninsula.
